context.why: Fourth story of FS-030. Accepted so far: US1 (LocatedRecord fields location/location_elevation/location_uncertainty on Sample and Measurement, Organization.location point, Person has none, the location input, Point removed), US3 (measurement's own and effective location), US2 (lookups and spatial coverage). This story puts locations into the REST API (plan D9): a read-only GeoJSONPointField in fairdm/api/serializers.py that, given the record, returns {'type': 'Point', 'coordinates': [lon, lat]} with location_elevation appended as a third coordinate when set, or None; annotated for drf-spectacular as a GeoJSON point. BaseSampleSerializer and BaseMeasurementSerializer add 'location' and 'location_uncertainty' to common_fields and Meta.fields; OrganizationListSerializer (and so OrganizationSerializer) adds 'location' without elevation. Person serializers carry no location. A measurement returns only its own location, never its sample's (decisions D4). All location fields are read-only (decisions D14): a create or partial change that sends location, location_elevation or location_uncertainty leaves them as they were and never raises the database constraint.
spec_sections: Clarifications (API returns what the record holds)
prior_decisions: D1: a location is a value on each record, never a shared row. No Location model, no get_or_create.
D2: Organization holds a plain point, a Person holds none. Contributor.location is removed.
D8: no data migration — existing Point data is not carried across.
D12: field names are location, location_elevation, location_uncertainty.

FR-009: a sample type shows the location input only when its registration's fields list location. The demo's RockSample registration is to list location (as the approved prototype did); WaterSample does not.

D3 (decisions): a measurement falls back to its sample's location only for a viewer who may open the sample (Sample.objects.visible_to(user)); for anyone else a measurement with no location of its own has none.
D16: location constraints are listed in each concrete model's own Meta (location_constraints()), not on LocatedRecord.Meta.
D4 (decisions): the API returns a record's own location, never the effective one; a harvester follows the sample link.
D14: location fields are read-only in the API.
RFC 7946: WGS 84, longitude first; uncertainty is not part of GeoJSON and sits beside the geometry as location_uncertainty in metres.
Do not build import/export columns or organization forms: later stories.

acceptance.given_when_then: A located sample returns a GeoJSON Point with [lon, lat] (plus elevation third when recorded) and location_uncertainty beside it; a sample with none and a measurement with no own location return null; an organization returns its point; a person carries no location; the OpenAPI schema describes the field as a GeoJSON point; a create or partial change sending location fields leaves the stored location unchanged.
GeoJSONPointField and the serializer fields exist per plan D9, read-only.
locations.md and the API documentation page describe the location shape with an example; FS-011's spec text no longer says GeoJSON is not part of the API.
